title: Personal Assistant
description:
We are looking for a calm, patient, empathetic and reliable Personal Assistant to provide one-to-one support to a young adult male with severe learning disabilities.

This is a rewarding role for someone who genuinely enjoys supporting others and is confident in providing patient, respectful and engaging care.

Support will be provided primarily within the family home, alongside regular outings and activities within the local community and across the London area and beyond.

The person you will be supporting is full of personality and enjoys getting out and about, experiencing different activities and adventures. A willingness to actively engage with and encourage these interests is therefore an important part of the role.

The role

Following a period of shadowing and appropriate training, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing support with meals, including physical assistance and close supervision.
- Providing wheelchair assistance when out in the community.
- Assisting with personal care.
- Offering reassurance and calm support during periods of anxiety or distress.
- Using appropriate diversion and de-escalation techniques with patience and understanding.
- Encouraging participation in activities and interests they enjoy.
- Maintaining awareness of safety and providing appropriate monitoring and supervision.
- Supporting a positive, respectful and enjoyable environment both at home and within the community.
- 3/4 Days p.wk-including some weekends Average of 8 hours p.day

About you

The successful candidate will ideally be:
- Naturally calm, patient and empathetic.
- Friendly, warm and respectful in their approach.
- A confident communicator who can build a positive one-to-one relationship.
- Patient and able to remain composed when faced with anxiety or challenging situations.
- Comfortable providing physical and personal care.
- Engaging and willing to participate in activities and outings.
- Reliable, responsible and committed to providing consistent support.
- Willing to complete all mandatory training and ongoing development required for the role.

Previous experience as a Personal Assistant or supporting someone with learning disabilities would be highly valued, although the right attitude, patience and commitment are equally important.

Essential requirements
- Must have the right to work in the UK.
- An Enhanced DBS check will be required for the successful candidate.
- References will be requested and checked as part of the recruitment process.
- Willingness to undertake the required training.

How to apply

If you feel this role could be right for you, please email a covering letter explaining why you feel you would be suitable for the position, along with details of your relevant experience.

We are looking for someone who will become a trusted and valued part of this individual s support team and family life.

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
description:
Behaviour Support Assistant - KS3 to KS5 (SEN School)
Location: Specialist SEN School
Start Date: ASAP
Contract: Full-time, Temporary
Pay: 100- 125 per day (negotiable)
Hours: 8:30am - 4:00pm, Monday to Friday

We are seeking a confident, resilient and highly adaptable Behaviour Support Assistant to join a specialist SEN school supporting students aged 11-19 (KS3-KS5). This is a full-time role suited to someone with previous SEN school experience who thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and is comfortable responding to changing needs throughout the school day.

You will play a key role in supporting behaviour, engagement and emotional regulation across the school, working closely with teaching and pastoral staff.

The Role:
- Provide in-class behaviour support across multiple lessons and departments
- Respond quickly and professionally to behaviour support requests from staff
- Deliver short-term, targeted interventions on a 1:1 or 1:2 basis
- Support students with regulation, engagement and transitions
- Assist with off-site activities, including swimming and outdoor learning
- Follow changing timetables and priorities with flexibility and professionalism

The Ideal Candidate Will:
- Have experience working in a specialist SEN school (essential)
- Be flexible and confident supporting different age groups and needs
- Be physically active and able to support students with complex needs
- Demonstrate resilience and confidence managing behaviours that challenge
- Communicate effectively and work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
- Maintain a calm, professional and proactive approach at all times

Please note: Mainstream-only experience or sports coaching backgrounds are not suitable for this role.

This is a rewarding opportunity to make a meaningful impact in a specialist setting supporting young people with complex needs.

Apply now or get in touch to discuss suitable candidates for this Behaviour Support Assistant role.

title: Residential Support Worker
description:
Are you an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work?

We are currently recruiting experienced and reliable Residential Support Workers to support vulnerable children and young people across a range of residential care settings.

The young people you will support may have experienced trauma or difficult life circumstances and may present with challenging behaviours, autism, emotional and behavioural difficulties and complex support needs.

This is a rewarding opportunity for caring and resilient individuals who want to make a positive difference while enjoying the flexibility of agency work.

The Role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide high-quality care and support to children and young people, helping them feel safe, supported and valued.

Your responsibilities may include:
- Providing day-to-day care and support to vulnerable children and young people
- Building positive and trusting relationships
- Supporting young people with their daily routines and individual needs
- Engaging children in activities, hobbies and interests
- Supporting emotional wellbeing and personal development
- Managing and responding appropriately to challenging behaviours
- Supporting children with autism and other additional needs
- Following individual care plans and risk assessments
- Maintaining professional boundaries and providing consistent support

Every shift will be different, and you may work with young people with a range of needs and backgrounds. You will need to be adaptable, patient and able to remain calm and professional in challenging situations.

Flexible Agency Shifts

Agency work gives you the flexibility to work around your existing commitments, with shifts available across a range of residential childcare settings.

You must be able to work flexible hours, which may include long day shifts, weekends, bank holidays and sleep ins. Flexibility is essential, as shift patterns and requirements will vary depending on the home and the needs of the young people.

About You

We are looking for people who are:
- Calm and emotionally resilient
- Confident supporting children with challenging behaviours
- Comfortable working with children and young people with autism and additional needs
- Reliable and professional
- Able to adapt to different care environments
- Passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of vulnerable young people

Requirements

To be considered for these agency opportunities, you will need:
- To be 21 years of age or over
- At least 6 months' experience working with children or young people in a residential setting
- A clean UK driving licence
- The flexibility to work long days, weekends and sleep-in shifts when required
- A genuine commitment to working with vulnerable children and young people

Why Work With Us?
- Flexible temporary agency shifts
- Opportunity to work across a variety of residential childcare settings
- Gain experience working with children with a range of complex needs
- Build your experience within the residential childcare sector
- Potential opportunities for ongoing and permanent work
- Support from your dedicated recruitment team
- Opportunity to make a genuine difference to vulnerable young people's lives

If you're an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work and are passionate about supporting children and young people, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to discuss available shifts and opportunities in your area.

title: Family & Community Support Worker
description:
We are looking for a caring, reliable and confident Family & Community Support Worker to support children and young people and give families some much-needed support and respite.

This is a role where no two days are the same. You could be supporting a child out in the community, taking them to activities, helping them try something new, or simply spending time with them while giving their parent or carer respite.

We are particularly looking for someone who has experience supporting children and young people with Autism, ADHD and other neurodivergent needs, including children who may sometimes display challenging or physical behaviour.

What will you be doing?

The role will vary depending on the child and their individual needs, but may include:
- Supporting children and young people in the community
- Taking them to activities, parks, clubs and places they enjoy
- Providing respite for parents and carers
- Helping children build confidence and independence
- Supporting emotional regulation and behaviour
- Helping children take part in activities and experiences
- Building a positive and trusting relationship with the child
- Following individual support plans and strategies
- Communicating with parents/carers about how the child has been
- Keeping the child safe and making sure they are supported in a way that works for them

The person we're looking for

We are looking for someone who is patient, calm, compassionate and genuinely enjoys working with children and young people.

You should be someone who can stay calm when things become difficult and understand that behaviour is often a way of communicating that something isn't right.

Experience with Autism, ADHD, SEND, neurodiversity, challenging behaviour or physical behaviour would be really valuable.

We're looking for someone who:
- Is kind, patient and understanding
- Can remain calm under pressure
- Is confident supporting children who may display physical or challenging behaviour
- Has experience with, or a good understanding of, Autism and ADHD
- Is reliable and dependable
- Is comfortable working independently
- Can think on their feet and adapt to different situations
- Has good communication skills
- Understands the importance of safeguarding and professional boundaries
- Can build a genuine relationship with a child
- Doesn't give up when things don't go to plan

Why work with us?

We know that flexibility is important, which is why we offer flexible hours around your availability and the needs of the families we support.

You'll also receive weekly pay and have the opportunity to do work that genuinely makes a difference.

This can be a great role for someone who wants work that fits around their life, whether you're looking for additional hours, part-time work or something more regular.

You won't be sitting behind a desk all day. You'll be out in the community, getting to know the children and families you support and helping them have positive experiences.

Experience we'd love to see

Experience in any of the following would be beneficial:

Autism ADHD SEND Neurodiversity Challenging Behaviour Physical Behaviour Positive Behaviour Support Family Support Respite Social Care Education Youth Work

DBS & Safeguarding

As you will be working directly with children and young people, an Enhanced DBS check is required for this role.

Appropriate references and safeguarding checks will also be completed as part of the recruitment process.

If this sounds like you

If you're someone who genuinely enjoys helping others, doesn't panic when things get difficult and wants to do work that has a real purpose, we'd love to hear from you.

Please get in touch to find out more about the role and the families we currently have support available for.

title: Care Assistant - Maternity Cover
company: Viewpoint Housing Association Ltd - Agency - Temporary
description:
About Us

At Viewpoint, people matter, not just our residents and tenants but our staff. We are a registered non-profit making organisation providing a range of general needs housing, supported housing and care services for older people in Edinburgh, the Lothians and Fife. Established in 1947, our primary objective is to improve the quality of life and well-being of our care home residents and tenants through promoting independence, enabling choice and offering peace of mind in a safe, secure and supported environment.

About the Role

As a Care Assistant, you play a key role in the life and individual wellbeing of our residents, ensuring that their physical, emotional and social needs are met and care is delivered to the highest standard in accordance with their care plans. You assist with all day to day aspects of personal care needs including washing, dressing, assisting with meals. You also help to provide mental and physical stimulation by participating in recreational and social activities with our residents.

You will have up to 3 weeks induction when you will work closely with an experienced member of our staff team, to get to know our residents, the rest of the care home team and other people within our organisation. You will be supported and trained in a range of topics, including Fire Awareness, Moving & Handling, Infection Prevention & Control, Health & Safety, Safeguarding, Promoting Excellence in Dementia, Palliative & End of Life Care, Record Keeping (using our information recording system) and Data Protection (GDPR). Thereafter, you will continue to be supported in your learning and development to grow and thrive in your role

We require you to register with the Scottish Social Services Council (SSSC) and to maintain the registration throughout your employment. We also require you join the Adult Protection of Vulnerable Groups (PVG) Scheme, and cover this cost for you.

About You

You will ideally have knowledge and understanding of the difficulties that can be experienced by older people. You might have gained this through providing support in a community setting, through experience in your own family, or through another relevant environment.

You are kind and respectful, always focused on preserving the dignity and self-respect for those you are or would be caring for. You have excellent verbal and written communication skills and are able to work effectively with a variety of people from a variety of backgrounds. You are keen to support and drive the development of a positive working culture.

Benefits

We offer a generous reward package which includes:
- 7 weeks holidays including public holidays
- Flexible shift patterns
- Enhanced overtime rates
- SSSC (renewal paid)
- Attractive pension scheme
- Life insurance (death in service benefit)
- Free uniforms
- An up to 3 week Induction Programme where you work alongside a colleague and are supervised and supported in practice to take responsibility for your work.
- Wellbeing support (Employee Assistance Programme)
- Bluelight Discounts

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

No experience necessary! Are you patient, empathetic and committed to helping people live fulfilling lives We are seeking a caring Support Worker to help autistic adults build confidence, develop skills and enjoy greater independence in their communities.

Position: Support Worker (Vocational and Community Services)
Salary: £13.45 per hour
Location: Hunslet and Armley, Leeds
Working hours: Monday to Friday, typically 9:00am 4:00pm, with some flexibility required to accommodate support sessions starting earlier or finishing later.

About the role

Make a positive difference every day by supporting autistic adults to achieve their personal goals and feel included and valued within their communities.

Working across day and outreach settings, you will provide person-centred support that respects each individual s choices, interests and preferred ways of communicating.

Key responsibilities include:
- Supporting people to develop practical skills, confidence and self-esteem.
- Identifying opportunities for personal development and community participation.
- Promoting physical and emotional wellbeing.
- Helping individuals plan their own support and make decisions about their lives.
- Supporting communication, social understanding and positive relationships.
- Helping people develop coping strategies through Positive Behaviour Support.
- Providing practical and emotional support, maintaining accurate records and following safeguarding procedures.

You will work closely with colleagues, families and other professionals to deliver consistent, thoughtful support.

About you

You will be patient, empathetic and committed to helping people live fulfilling lives. You will respect individual differences and bring a positive, non-judgemental approach to your work.

You will also have:
- Good communication and interpersonal skills.
- The ability to work well within a team and use your initiative.
- Basic IT skills to complete records and communicate with colleagues.
- A flexible approach and willingness to undertake training.
- A commitment to equality, inclusion and safeguarding.

Experience supporting autistic people or people with learning disabilities, an understanding of person-centred support, and relevant care qualifications would be welcome but are not essential.

About the organisation

This specialist charity works to create a more autism-friendly society through practical support, campaigning and promoting greater understanding of autism.

You will join a supportive team with access to training, development and progression opportunities. Benefits include a pension scheme, healthcare scheme, sick pay, death in service benefit, an Employee Assistance Programme, and employee recognition and referral programmes.

The organisation welcomes applications from all sections of the community. Successful applicants will be subject to an Enhanced DBS check and pre-employment checks.

Other roles you may have experience of could include Autism Support Worker, Community Support Worker, Outreach Support Worker, Learning Disability Support Worker, Day Services Support Worker, Care Worker or Support Assistant.

Please note this role is advertised by the recruitment agency acting for the client Not For Profit People.

title: Floating Support Worker
description:
Are you looking for a rewarding role where you can make a real difference?

We have a 40-hour per-week support worker role available in our Floating Support Team based in Hillingdon.

Our Hillingdon Mental Health Floating Support Team provides housing-related support to adults with mental health issues living in Hillingdon. Support is delivered in a variety of settings including service users homes, community settings and where relevant, in the service user s workplace or learning place.

Being a support worker is a very rewarding job. The role is often challenging but you can make a positive difference to someone s life- enabling them to become more independent brings feelings of accomplishment and satisfaction. It s a great career choice for those who enjoy a varied job role and lots of interaction with other agencies.

About the role: you will,
- deliver housing related support to customers in their own homes and in the community, including support with developing independent living skills, benefit maximisation, accessing and attending health appointments, accessing and engaging with social and learning activities, volunteering and community engagement.
- support with finding and securing alternative accommodation.
- support customers in setting up and maintaining a home / tenancy, including support with maintenance, repairs, payment of rent and arrears, and being a good neighbour.
- You will work with 13 customers using a strength-based, person-centred approach. We support our customers using the recovery model and co-produce SMART support plans with them to enable them to achieve their goals, sustain independence and enjoy a good quality of life. You will be responsible for ensuring support plans and risk assessments are in date.
- minimise unplanned and emergency hospital admissions for mental health relapse by offering general support, including emotional support and advice, support with monitoring own health and well-being and signposting to health services.

The service operates Monday Friday 9am to 5pm, A full UK driving licence and access to a car are essential for this role."

Benefits you will receive with this role.
- Support and Leadership
- Training and development opportunities
- Company healthcare scheme
- 30 days annual leave (included bank holidays)
- Contributory pension
- Sick Pay

This post requires employment references and clearance by the Disclosure & Barring Service.

- A generous pension - we will contribute up to 8% and life assurance cover up to 3x Pensionable Salary (T&Cs apply)

What you'll do:

- Develop reliable, professionally boundaried relationships with customers who may be distressed, guarded, ambivalent or difficult to engage.
- Monitor mental state, behaviour, dynamic risk and protective factors and communicate significant changes promptly.

title: Family Support Worker
description:
Randstad is proud to partner with a leading care charity in England and Wales, to recruit a passionate Family Support Worker. If you are driven by making a difference for grand-parents, siblings, and family members stepping up to raise children, this role offers a rewarding opportunity to deliver pioneering 1-to-1 support.

Role Snapshot

Role Title: Family Support Worker

Salary: 29,000 per annum pro rata ( 23,200 actual)

Working Hours: Part-time (0.8 FTE / 28 hours per week)

Contract: Fixed-term until August 2027

Location: Newham (co-located in local authority hubs with home visits, hybrid working & occasional head office visits)

Generous Leave: 24 days annual leave (based on 30 days FTE) + pro rata bank holidays

About the Opportunity

This is a unique chance to work at the forefront of a pioneering Randomised Controlled Trial (RCT) pilot programme-the Connected programme. Designed to deliver intensive, structured 6-month support, the programme helps kinship carers stabilise placements, navigate complex systems, and access vital services.

As a Family Support Worker, you will manage an active caseload of approximately 20 families at a time (around 40 across the year). Combining relational casework with high-quality data collection, your efforts will help build a strong evidence base to transform kinship care nationwide.

What You Will Do

Direct 1-to-1 Support: Provide emotional and practical guidance to carers in their homes and local communities using the Connected Intervention Protocol.

Support Groups & Events: Establish and facilitate monthly support groups and coordinate celebratory family events.

Multi-Agency Collaboration: Work closely with local authority teams, social workers, schools, health services, and community partners to advocate for families.

Data & Casework Recording: Maintain accurate, timely CRM records (Salesforce) and complete SMART goal assessments to support trial evaluation.

Safeguarding & Risk Management: Follow established safeguarding policies and risk assessment frameworks with full support from designated safeguarding leads.

What We Are Looking For
Essential Criteria:

Proven experience supporting vulnerable families or carers, completing needs assessments, and developing support plans.

Experience in community-focused casework and facilitating peer or support groups.

Demonstrated ability to build trusting relationships while maintaining professional boundaries.

Strong IT and administration skills, including experience using CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce) for case management.

Knowledge of trauma-informed and strengths-based approaches to family support.

Clear understanding of safeguarding procedures and child protection practices.

Strong commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Right to work in the UK and willingness to travel within Newham and surrounding areas.

Desirable Criteria:

Lived experience of kinship care.

Background in social care, early help, or children & family support services.

Existing knowledge of statutory policies and support options for kinship families.

How to Apply

To apply for this role through Randstad, please submit your CV along with responses to the following 5 screening questions (using real-world examples where possible):

1. Motivation: Why do you want to work as a Family Support Worker on the Connected programme, and how does this role align with your values and experience?

2. Assessment & Direct Support: Describe a time you supported a family facing complex challenges. How did you assess their needs and prioritize support?

3. Partnership Working: Tell us about a situation where you collaborated with external professionals (e.g., social workers, schools) to support a family.

4. Safeguarding: Give an example of when you had safety or wellbeing concerns regarding a child or family. What steps did you take

5. Casework & Data Management: How have you successfully managed a caseload while maintaining accurate data records?

Randstad Care acts as an employment business when supplying temporary staff and as an employment agency when introducing candidates for permanent employment with a client. Randstad Care is an equal opportunities employer and decisions are made on merits alone.

Did you know that Randstad Care have been awarded a place on the National Clinical Staffing Framework for the NHS? This means we will be able to bring you more opportunities within nursing & midwifery and clinical staffing.

title: Residential Support Worker
description:
Are you an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work?

We are currently recruiting experienced and reliable Residential Support Workers to support vulnerable children and young people across a range of residential care settings.

The young people you will support may have experienced trauma or difficult life circumstances and may present with challenging behaviours, autism, emotional and behavioural difficulties and complex support needs.

This is a rewarding opportunity for caring and resilient individuals who want to make a positive difference while enjoying the flexibility of agency work.

The Role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide high-quality care and support to children and young people, helping them feel safe, supported and valued.

Your responsibilities may include:
- Providing day-to-day care and support to vulnerable children and young people
- Building positive and trusting relationships
- Supporting young people with their daily routines and individual needs
- Engaging children in activities, hobbies and interests
- Supporting emotional wellbeing and personal development
- Managing and responding appropriately to challenging behaviours
- Supporting children with autism and other additional needs
- Following individual care plans and risk assessments
- Maintaining professional boundaries and providing consistent support

Every shift will be different, and you may work with young people with a range of needs and backgrounds. You will need to be adaptable, patient and able to remain calm and professional in challenging situations.

Flexible Agency Shifts

Agency work gives you the flexibility to work around your existing commitments, with shifts available across a range of residential childcare settings.

You must be able to work flexible hours, which may include long day shifts, weekends, bank holidays and sleep ins. Flexibility is essential, as shift patterns and requirements will vary depending on the home and the needs of the young people.

About You

We are looking for people who are:
- Calm and emotionally resilient
- Confident supporting children with challenging behaviours
- Comfortable working with children and young people with autism and additional needs
- Reliable and professional
- Able to adapt to different care environments
- Passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of vulnerable young people

Requirements

To be considered for these agency opportunities, you will need:
- To be 21 years of age or over
- At least 6 months' experience working with children or young people in a residential setting
- A clean UK driving licence
- The flexibility to work long days, weekends and sleep-in shifts when required
- A genuine commitment to working with vulnerable children and young people

Why Work With Us?
- Flexible temporary agency shifts
- Opportunity to work across a variety of residential childcare settings
- Gain experience working with children with a range of complex needs
- Build your experience within the residential childcare sector
- Potential opportunities for ongoing and permanent work
- Support from your dedicated recruitment team
- Opportunity to make a genuine difference to vulnerable young people's lives

If you're an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work and are passionate about supporting children and young people, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to discuss available shifts and opportunities in your area.
